src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197: Changing existing span-buf:s: Redis keys from sets to sorted sets without migration or a new namespace causes WRONGTYPE errors for buffered data and makes old and new consumers incompatible during mixed-version deployments, breaking insertion and flushing.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result passes negative slice indices directly to a Django queryset in the advanced negative-offset branch, causing request failures because Django rejects negative indexing; invalid offsets must be rejected or traversal implemented using supported queries.

goldens.comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch in get_result() passes cursor.offset directly as start_offset to queryset slicing when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0.
In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.
OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses floor/ceil on a datetime key (order_by='-datetime'), causing TypeError.
Accessing .has_global_access on organization_context.member can raise an AttributeError when organization_context is None, particularly for non-superuser non-member users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197: Changing existing span-buf:s: Redis keys from sets to sorted sets without migration or a new namespace causes WRONGTYPE errors for buffered data and makes old and new consumers incompatible during mixed-version deployments, breaking insertion and flushing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows Redis commands changing from set operations (sadd, scard, sscan, sunionstore) to sorted set operations (zadd, zcard, zscan, zunionstore) on the same key pattern 'span-buf:s:{project_and_trace}:{span_id}'. In buffer.py line 197, p.zadd() replaces p.sadd(). In the Lua script add-buffer.lua, scard/sunionstore are replaced with zcard/zunionstore. If existing Redis keys contain set data and new code tries sorted set operations on them, Redis will return WRONGTYPE errors. During a rolling deployment, old consumers would write sets while new consumers expect sorted sets, causing incompatibility. There's no migration strategy or new key namespace visible in the diff.
